# Git, worktrees and commits

<!-- orca-setup:begin -->
<!-- Generated by orca-setup from .orca-setup.json; change that file or the kit, not this block. -->

## Worktrees

- One worktree per plan, under `.worktrees/` (git-ignored), on branch `task/NNN-slug`.
- Created only through Orca, from the main checkout, so the setup in `orca.yaml` runs (git hooks,
  dependencies):

  ```bash
  orca worktree create --name NNN-slug --repo path:/Users/serhii/Developer/emdash-images --base-branch main --setup run --json
  ```

  Never `git worktree add`: setup would not run.
- Removed only after the branch is merged, with `./scripts/orca/remove-worktree.sh <worktree>`
  (prints `REMOVE OK`; it runs the `archive` script of `orca.yaml`, if any). Orca may delete the
  branch on removal, so never remove an unmerged one.

## Branches and merging

- `main` holds only reviewed work with passing gates.
- Executors commit on `task/NNN-slug`, one commit per task; in a fix round they amend their own
  task's commit.
- The run session merges a finished plan from the main checkout with
  `git merge --no-ff task/NNN-slug`, one plan at a time. A conflict goes back to an executor or to
  the user.
- Only the user pushes. Nobody rebases or resets `main`, deletes branches by hand, or
  force-pushes; agents never run `git push`, `gh` or `git remote`.

## Commits

- **Author:** the user. Git uses the user's identity; no AI author, `Co-authored-by` or
  "Generated with/by" line.
- **Signer:** 1Password signs every commit. Never turn signing off. In a worktree
  `git log --show-signature` may print `No signature` when `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` is not
  set; look for the `gpgsig` block in `git cat-file -p HEAD` instead.
- **Message:** an imperative subject of at most 72 characters, a blank line, then a short body that
  says what changed and why. Merge commits keep Git's default subject.
- **Enforced by** `.githooks/commit-msg` for every committer (`core.hooksPath .githooks`; `orca.yaml`
  sets it in each worktree, the user once in the main checkout), and by
  `scripts/orca/check-commits.sh` at the merge gate, which re-checks signatures and
  messages because `--no-verify` or `--no-gpg-sign` would skip the hook.
- **How to run it:** `git add` in one call, then the commit as a standalone command with `-m` per
  paragraph:

  ```bash
  git commit -m "Add the hero block" -m "Renders the hero from the design."
  ```

  No heredoc, `cd`, redirect or `&&`, and plain double-quoted messages. Only a
  command that starts with `git commit` or `git merge` leaves the sandbox, where the signer can
  reach its agent; anything else fails to sign.
